project.name: libxml2
project.fuzz_target: fuzz/xml reader path via staged run_xml_one harness

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free against this preserved vulnerable checkout. The staged patch edits `buf.c:xmlBufResetInput` to clear `input->base/cur/end` when `buf == NULL` or `buf->error` is set.

classification.classification_note: The reproduced failure is a heap-use-after-free read in libxml2's error-reporting path. The staged fuzz container first stores attacker-controlled main-entity and external-entity bodies in `xmlFuzzReadEntities()`, then the main entity expands `%nitf;` and `xmlFuzzEntityLoader()` materializes the stored `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd` bytes as an `xmlParserInputBuffer`. While `xmlLoadEntityContent()` reads that buffer, `xmlParserInputBufferGrow()` successfully reallocates it at least once, freeing the old heap region that `xmlParserInput.base/cur/end` still reference until the reset call after the grow loop. A later grow fails, `xmlBufResetInput()` returns early on `buf->error` without clearing those aliases, and `xmlReportError()` immediately calls `xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal()` on the stale `xmlParserInput`, which reads bytes from the freed region.

bug_description.original: A heap-use-after-free exists in libxml2's error reporting: xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal (error.c) can read from parser input pointers that reference freed heap memory when invoked via xmlReportError/__xmlRaiseError. This results in reads of deallocated memory during parsing (e.g., while handling entities or external subsets), leading to crashes or other undefined behavior and potentially enabling exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: The staged `fuzz/xml` witness is a libxml2 entity-container input: it begins with a 4-byte parser-options word and a 4-byte max-allocation word, then `xmlFuzzReadEntities()` stores a main XML entity and a second entity named `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd` in the fuzz entity table. The main entity's internal subset declares `% nitf SYSTEM "dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd";` and expands `%nitf;`, so `xmlStringDecodeEntitiesInt()` reaches `xmlLoadEntityContent()` and `xmlFuzzEntityLoader()` materializes the stored external parameter-entity bytes as a parser input buffer. The saved ASan trace proves that during `xmlLoadEntityContent()` one successful `xmlParserInputBufferGrow()` path reallocates the entity buffer and frees the old 8193-byte region, but a later grow returns `res < 0`. Vulnerable `xmlBufResetInput()` then executes with `buf->error` set and returns without rebinding or clearing `input->base`, `input->cur`, and `input->end`. `xmlFatalErr()` reports the failure through `__xmlRaiseError()` and `xmlReportError()`, which selects the same external-entity parser input and calls `xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal()`. The saved crash is the loop at `error.c:210` dereferencing `*cur` from the freed region. The fix adds the missing stale-pointer invalidation in `xmlBufResetInput()` by setting `input->base = input->cur = input->end = BAD_CAST ""` on the error path before returning.

source.description: First project-side statement on the witnessed path that stores attacker-controlled testcase bytes into vulnerability-relevant state. `xmlFuzzReadEntities()` preserves each entity body and byte length in the fuzz entity table here; the first iteration becomes the main entity later parsed for `%nitf;`, and a later iteration stores the external entity body later loaded through `xmlFuzzEntityLoader()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` strings show a main XML entity with an internal subset that expands `%nitf;` and a separate entry keyed by `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd`. This assignment stores those exact entity bodies and lengths in the table consumed later by the parser and loader.

root_cause.description: Patch-matching missing lifetime repair. When the external-entity buffer carries `buf->error`, vulnerable `xmlBufResetInput()` returns immediately and leaves the parser input's `base/cur/end` aliases unchanged even though they may still point to a heap region already freed by an earlier successful `realloc` in the same grow loop.
root_cause.note: The staged fix splits this guard and, on the `buf == NULL || buf->error` path, writes `input->base = input->cur = input->end = BAD_CAST ""` before returning.

sink.description: Crash sink. Error reporting scans the current parser input line using `cur = input->cur` and `len = input->end - cur`; on the witnessed path those fields still reference freed external-entity storage, so the loop reads from deallocated heap memory.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 1` at this line on `0x525000011900`, the start of a freed 8193-byte region.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific parser gate. The witness main entity must reach a `<!DOCTYPE ... [` declaration with an internal subset so the later `%nitf;` parameter-entity path is parsed instead of stopping after the prolog.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzz container stores each attacker-controlled entity body and its byte length in the entity table here. The first stored record becomes `fuzzData.mainEntity`, and the later `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd` record is what `xmlFuzzEntityLoader()` retrieves and passes into `xmlParserInputBufferCreateMem()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The strings extracted from the staged `poc` show both the main XML entity and an external entity keyed by `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd`; this statement preserves those exact bytes and lengths as the parser-visible source of the later dangling parser-input buffer.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged fuzz container is decoded into per-URL entity records: the first record becomes the main XML entity, and a later record stores the external entity body for `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd`.
The main entity is admitted into the internal subset parser, its `%nitf;` parameter-entity reference is resolved, and the validating/load predicate dispatches into `xmlLoadEntityContent()`.
The external entity `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd` is looked up in the fuzz entity table, materialized as an `xmlParserInputBuffer`, rebound into `input->base/cur/end`, and pushed as the current parser input.

While reading the external entity, one grow successfully `realloc`s and frees the old heap buffer, then a later grow fails; the final `xmlBufResetInput()` sees `buf->error` and returns without clearing the now-stale parser-input aliases.

The grow failure is reported immediately, `xmlReportError()` chooses the current external-entity input for context printing, and `xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal()` reads from the freed buffer through stale `input->cur/base/end` pointers.

fine_trace.note: Source. `xmlFuzzReadEntities()` stores attacker-controlled entity bytes and their length into the fuzz entity table. On the witnessed first iteration, these bytes are the main XML entity later parsed for `%nitf;`.

The first stored entity record is marked as the main XML document. This preserves the exact body whose internal subset later declares `<!ENTITY % nitf SYSTEM "dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd">` and expands `%nitf;`.
On a later loop iteration, the same storage path preserves the attacker-controlled external entity under URL `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd`, making its body and length available for later loader lookup.

depends_on.via: later url/body strings from the same testcase stream

fine_trace.note: While parsing the admitted main entity's internal subset, libxml2 consumes the attacker-controlled `%nitf;` reference and resolves it to the external parameter entity object.
Because the referenced parameter entity still has no in-memory content and the witnessed option state satisfies this predicate, parsing `%nitf;` takes the branch that loads external entity bytes.
The external-entity loader resolves the requested URL to the fuzz-supplied entity-table entry. On this witness, the lookup key is `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd`.
The fuzz-supplied external entity bytes are materialized as a libxml2 parser input buffer backed by heap storage. ASan's allocation stack points to this creation path.
Before the bulk read loop starts, libxml2 binds `input->base/cur/end` to the external-entity buffer and pushes this stream as the current parser input that later error reporting will inspect.

On at least one witnessed grow, `xmlRealloc` moves the entity buffer and frees the previous heap region. The parser-input aliases from step 8 are not refreshed during the loop, so they still point at that freed region until the later reset call.

On a later iteration of the same external-entity read loop, `xmlBufGrow()` sees `buf->error` after the failed grow attempt and `xmlParserInputBufferGrow()` records that failure as `in->error = XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY` before returning `-1`, setting up the stale-pointer reset failure that follows.
After the read loop stops, libxml2 calls `xmlBufResetInput()` to refresh the current parser input from the possibly reallocated buffer before handling the grow result.

Root cause. After the failed grow, the post-loop reset runs with `buf->error` set, so vulnerable `xmlBufResetInput()` exits without rebinding or clearing the parser-input aliases that still target the freed region from step 9.
The failed grow is reported immediately while the current parser input is still the external entity whose `base/cur/end` fields were left stale by step 12.
Error reporting selects the current parser input from the parser context. On this path that input is the external entity stream whose `base/cur/end` pointers were left dangling.
Sink. `cur` is initialized from `input->cur`, and the loop reads bytes and computes lengths from the freed entity buffer region left dangling by step 12, producing the saved heap-use-after-free read.

poc.trigger: Run the staged `run_xml_one` reader harness on the saved `poc`. The witness causes libxml2 to parse a main internal subset that expands `%nitf;`, load external parameter entity `dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd`, successfully grow and move its input buffer at least once, then hit a later grow failure and crash in `xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal()` while reporting that error.

format.name: libxml2 fuzz/xml entity-container testcase
format.contract: The file must follow `fuzz/xml.c` and `fuzz/fuzz.c` container layout: 4 bytes of parser options, 4 bytes of max-allocation limit, then backslash-newline terminated URL/body pairs parsed by `xmlFuzzReadEntities()`. This witness needs a main XML entity whose internal subset declares `% nitf SYSTEM "dtds/nitf-2-5.dtd"` and expands `%nitf;`, plus an external entity entry for that exact URL whose body is the long malformed DTD fragment observed in the staged `poc`. The options word must leave the `xmlStringDecodeEntitiesInt()` load predicate true so `xmlLoadEntityContent()` runs, and the max-allocation field must produce the witnessed schedule of at least one successful buffer-growing `realloc` followed by a later grow failure before error reporting.
